title: Jude and the Garden
premise: Quentin Joubert, a memory-thief hiding in plain sight as a charm-seller, has kept their gift secret for twenty years in a city that executes magic-users. When the crown's hunt begins, they flee with Jude, a gardener whose loyalty conceals a truth: Jude is the crown's informant, planted years ago to find them. Their only escape lies through a door into a country that was erased from maps and memory alike — a country Quentin once stole memories from and cannot remember stealing. To open it, Quentin must return what they took, including the piece of themselves that knows why the country fell, while Jude must choose between the crown that owns them and the person they have come to love. The door opens only when both truths are paid; Quentin survives diminished and nameless, Jude survives exiled and honest, and together they plant a garden on the far side of a border no one else will ever cross.
about_author: Marguerite Crane is the pen name of a former botanical illustrator who spent a decade cataloguing extinct gardens before turning to fiction. She writes about memory, borders, and the things people bury to stay alive.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A day in the market: Quentin sells harmless trinkets, secretly harvesting small memories from willing customers to survive. Establishes the city's fear of magic and Quentin's careful loneliness. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Jude at the Gate
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Jude, a palace gardener, arrives with an order for charms for the royal conservatory — an impossible errand that smells like a trap. They banter; Quentin is charmed despite suspicion. Emotional beat: wary attraction.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Criers announce the Gift Hunt: all magic-users must register or die. The market empties around Quentin. That night they burn twenty years of ledgers. Emotional beat: terror crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: What Jude Knows
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, first time. Jude reports to a crown handler about Quentin's shop — revealing they've been informing for years under coercion. But they omit one detail to protect Quentin. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Knock at Midnight
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Soldiers raid the shop; Jude warns Quentin minutes before, betraying their handler. They flee together through the flooded cisterns beneath the city. Emotional beat: trust extended blindly.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the road east, the pair poses as pilgrims. Quentin notices Jude flinches at every checkpoint — too practiced. First seed of doubt. Emotional beat: intimacy shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: The Memory of Rain
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin steals a memory from a dying refugee and finds fragments of a green country that appears on no map — and feels an eerie recognition. Emotional beat: longing for something unnameable.

chapters.title: Handler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Flashback to how the crown recruited Jude: debt, a sick sister, a bargain. We learn Jude has hunted other gift-bearers before. Emotional beat: shame made concrete.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At a border town, registration lists are read aloud; a neighbor from the market is executed. Quentin realizes the hunt is personal — someone named them. Emotional beat: grief curdling into anger.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude nearly tells Quentin everything by firelight but instead asks what Quentin would do to someone who lied to save them. Quentin answers more gently than Jude deserves. Emotional beat: love complicating treachery.

chapters.title: Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In a mountain archive, an old woman recognizes Quentin's stolen-memory 'signature' — she says Quentin helped erase her homeland from every map. Quentin remembers nothing. Emotional beat: horror at one's own hands.

chapters.title: The Country With No Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The old woman describes the erased nation: it fed on memory itself, and the crown destroyed it rather than share borders with forgetting. Quentin's gift may be its last inheritance. Emotional beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Wolves in Livery
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Crown hunters corner them at a pass; Jude kills a soldier to save Quentin, crossing a line they can't return from. Emotional beat: the informant becomes fugitive.

chapters.title: What I Was Sent For
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Full confession: Jude was sent to confirm Quentin's gift and lead the hunters to them. Quentin walks away into the snow without a word. Emotional beat: devastation on both sides.

chapters.title: Alone Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Alone, Quentin discovers a locked memory inside themselves — sealed by their own younger hand — containing the location of the Door. Opening it requires a price. Emotional beat: bleak self-confrontation.

chapters.title: The Sister's Grave
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude visits their sister's grave en route to surrendering to the crown and finds the sister alive — the crown's hostage all along, the leash on Jude's loyalty. Emotional beat: rage replacing obedience.

chapters.title: Reunion by Force
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hunters capture Quentin; Jude turns coat publicly to infiltrate the escort, freeing Quentin in a bloody night skirmish. Neither apologizes yet. Emotional beat: forgiveness as action, not words.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The sealed memory opens partially: the Door out of the dead country demands returned memories — every theft Quentin ever made, plus one truth freely given. Emotional beat: accounting of a life.

chapters.title: Market of Stolen Things
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin tracks down former customers to return their memories, experiencing each life twice. Some refuse; one curses them. Emotional beat: restitution as penance.

chapters.title: Jude's Free Truth
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude gives the crown's secrets to a rebel cell — burning their last bridge home — because the Door needs 'one truth freely given' and Jude chooses to give theirs to Quentin instead. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: The Erased Capital
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the ruins of the nameless country: a city where buildings remember being gardens. The air eats at their memories. Emotional beat: awe laced with decay.

chapters.title: Gardens That Remember
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Among the ruins, Quentin finds their own childhood handwriting on a wall — proof they lived here before the erasure, before the theft of their own past. Emotional beat: vertigo of lost identity.

chapters.title: The Handler's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The crown handler, pursuing, offers Jude full pardon and their sister's freedom if they deliver Quentin at the Door. Jude pretends to accept. Emotional beat: double agent's cold sweat.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin returns the final stolen memories and feels their gift thinning — the power that defined them draining away. Who are they without it? Emotional beat: identity stripped bare.

chapters.title: The Door in the Hedge
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They find the Door: an archway of living thorn in the ruined palace garden, sealed, waiting for payment. Hunters arrive at the ridge behind them. Emotional beat: arrival and siege at once.

chapters.title: Siege of Thorns
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The garden itself defends them — the erased country's last magic answering Quentin's residual gift. But each defense costs Quentin more memory. Emotional beat: spending oneself to buy hours.

chapters.title: Jude's Choice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The handler calls Jude's bluff, holding the sister at knifepoint via messenger-mirror. Jude must choose: sister or Quentin, crown or truth. Emotional beat: the book's moral fulcrum.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jude refuses the crown and speaks their whole truth aloud at the Door — every betrayal, every year of coerced loyalty. The thorns drink the confession and begin to open. Emotional beat: honesty as sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Quentin Owes
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Door demands its final price: the sealed memory of why the country fell — Quentin, as a child, led the crown's cartographers here. Their survival began in betrayal too. Emotional beat: mirror to Jude's sin.

chapters.title: The Falling Country
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin relives the fall: the country chose to erase itself rather than be weaponized, sparing only the child who wept in the garden. Quentin gives the memory back willingly. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into understanding.

chapters.title: The Handler at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The handler breaches the garden as the Door opens; Jude fights them off, taking a wound meant for Quentin. The sister, freed by rebels, arrives to pull Jude back from death. Emotional beat: debts repaid in blood and rescue.

chapters.title: Through
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin steps through carrying almost nothing — no gift, few memories, Jude's hand. Behind them the country finishes dissolving, taking the Door forever. Emotional beat: passage as rebirth.

chapters.title: The Other Side
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A new land, real and unmapped. Jude wakes bandaged; Quentin sits beside them, half-remembering even Jude. Emotional beat: tenderness amid loss.

chapters.title: Nameless Again
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin cannot recall their own history and must decide whether to grieve or begin. They choose to introduce themselves to Jude as if for the first time. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from choice, not past.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude writes to the sister, knowing letters may never arrive across the closed border, and finds peace in the writing itself. Emotional beat: love that persists without guarantee.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring. They break ground on a garden using seeds Jude carried unknowingly from the palace conservatory — the erased country's flora, dormant for decades, sprouting. Emotional beat: hope made literal.

chapters.title: Visitors
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Other refugees from the hunt trickle through mountain passes, drawn by rumor of a garden beyond the map. Quentin, giftless, can only offer ordinary hospitality — and finds it enough. Emotional beat: purpose without power.

chapters.title: The Question of Going Back
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude admits they could try to reach the sister overland. Quentin tells them to go if they must. Jude stays — not out of debt, but desire. Emotional beat: loyalty freely chosen at last.

chapters.title: Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Autumn: first harvest festival in the settlement. Quentin remembers a fragment — not of theft or betrayal, but of their mother singing in this soil. Emotional beat: joy with roots in recovered truth.

chapters.title: Jude and the Garden
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. Years later, travelers tell of a garden at the edge of maps tended by two people: one who forgot everything, one who remembered too much. Final image: the two of them planting a tree whose fruit restores small kindnesses. Emotional beat: peace earned, theme resolved — truth and loyalty reconciled in shared cultivation.
